newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe arrives at Chirac office to resign.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe arrives at Chirac office to resign.

text.p: France's outgoing Prime Minister Alain Juppe arrived at President Jacques Chirac's office on Monday to hand in his government's resignation after a stinging electoral defeat.

Juppe drove to Chirac's Elysee palace from his offices on the other side of the Seine river. He said last week he would resign on Monday irrespective of the outcome of Sunday's runoff ballot in which the Socialist-led opposition won a majority in the National Assembly.

Juppe, like Chirac humiliated by the defeat of the centre-right coalition in Sunday's National Assembly election, was met on the steps of the Elysee Palace by the secretary-general of Chirac's office, Dominique de Villepin.

The conservative premier briefly turned to photographers waiting in the coutyard on his way in. The Socialist-led left won a majority in the 577-member National Assembly in election runoffs on Sunday.

Chirac has to receive Juppe's formal resignation and the final results of the parliamentary election, likely later on Monday morning, before naming Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin as prime minister, probably later in the day.
Jospin, who wants conditions on taking part in a single European currency, could then start work on forming a cabinet to rule in a hostile tandem with conservative Chirac.
